groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: India's Struggle for Independence treats early revolutionary activity as a response to Swadeshi's
decline, colonial repression and the impatience of young nationalists seeking immediate action.
The revolutionaries believed that assassination, bomb-making, arms procurement and planned mutiny could
break fear, inspire patriotic sacrifice and expose the vulnerability of colonial authority.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: Secret organisations such as Anushilan Samiti, Jugantar and Abhinav Bharat
combined physical training, ideological reading, oath-bound discipline and selective violence.
CAUTION: The strategy's central weakness was substituting heroic conspiracy for sustained mass mobilisation.
India House in London, Madame Cama in Europe and the Ghadar Party in North America made anti-colonial politics transnational.

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: Ghadar linked racial discrimination abroad, peasant-soldier migration, anti-imperial propaganda and First
World War opportunity into a plan for revolt in India.
The 1915 mutiny plan failed because British intelligence penetrated networks
and because revolutionary groups lacked coordinated mass support inside India.
